title: What it means that God comes down
source_text: Πότερον μὲν οὖν εἰσι περίοδοι καὶ κατὰ περιόδους κατακλυσμοὶ ἢ ἐκπυρώσεις, ἢ μὴ εἰσὶ, καὶ εἰ ἐπίσταται καὶ ταῦθ᾿ ὁ λόγος, ἐν πολλοῖς μὲν καὶ ἐν οἷς δὲ Σολομών φησι· „τί τὸ γεγονός; αὐτὸ τὸ γενησόμενον· καὶ τί τὸ πεποιημένον; αὐτὸ τὸ ποιηθησόμενον“ καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς, οὐ τοῦ παρόντος ἐστὶ καιροῦ λέγειν. ἀρκεῖ γὰρ μόνον ἐπισημειώσασθαι ὅτι ἀρχαιότατοι ἄνδρες γενόμενοι Μωϋσῆς καί τινες τῶν προφητῶν οὐ παρ᾿ ἑτέρων εἰλήφασι τὰ περὶ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου ἐκπυρώσεως ἀλλ᾿, εἰ χρὴ ἐπιστήσαντα τοῖς χρόνοις εἰπεῖν, μᾶλλον τούτων ἕτεροι παρακούσαντες καὶ μὴ ἀκριβώσαντες τὰ ὑπὸ τούτων λεγόμενα ἀνέπλασαν κατὰ περιόδους ταυτότητας καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτους τοῖς ἰδίοις ποιοῖς καὶ τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν αὐτοῖς. ἡμεῖς δὲ οὔτε τὸν κατακλυσμὸν οὔτε τὴν ἐκπύρωσιν κύκλοις καὶ ἀστέρων περιόδοις ἀνατίθεμεν, ἀλλὰ τὴν τούτων αἰτίαν φαμὲν εἶναι κακίαν ἐπὶ πλεῖον χεομένην καὶ καθαιρομένην κατακλυσμῷ ἢ ἐκπυ ρώσει. θεὸν δὲ καταβαίνοντα ἐὰν λέγωσιν αἱ προφητικαὶ φωναὶ τὸν φήσαντα· „οὐχὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐγὼ πληρῶ; λέγει κύριος,“ τροπολογοῦμεν. καταβαίνει γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἰδίου μεγέθους καὶ ὕψους, ὅτε τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ μάλιστα τῶν φαύλων οἰκονομεῖ. καὶ ὥσπερ ἡ συνήθεια συγκαταβαίνειν φησὶ τοῖς νηπίοις τοὺς διδασκάλους καὶ τοῖς ἄρτι προτραπεῖσιν ἐπὶ φιλοσοφίαν νέοις τοὺς σοφοὺς ἢ τοὺς προκόπτοντας οὐ τῷ σωματικῶς αὐτοὺς καταβαίνειν, οὕτως εἴ που λέγεται ἐν ταῖς θείαις γραφαῖς καταβαίνειν ὁ θεὸς, ἀνάλογον νοεῖται τῇ οὑτωσὶ χρωμένῃ τῷ ὀνόματι συνηθείᾳ, οὕτω δὲ καὶ ἀναβαίνειν.
pass_a_gloss: Whether there are periods and according to periods floods or conflagrations, or there are not, and whether the word (ὁ λόγος) also knows (ἐπίσταται) these things, both in many places and in those where Solomon says, 'What is the thing that has come to be (τὸ γεγονός)? The very thing that shall come to be. And what is the thing made (τὸ πεποιημένον)? The very thing that shall be made', and what follows (τὰ ἑξῆς), it is not of the present occasion (καιρός) to say. For it suffices only to note (ἐπισημειώσασθαι) that, being most ancient men, Moses and some of the prophets did not receive (εἰλήφασι) from others the things about the conflagration of the world, but, if one must say it having attended (ἐπιστήσαντα) to the times (χρόνοι), rather others, having misheard these and not having got exact (ἀκριβώσαντες) the things said by them, fashioned/invented (ἀνέπλασαν) according to periods identities (ταυτότητας) and things indistinguishable (ἀπαραλλάκτους) in their individual qualities (τοῖς ἰδίοις ποιοῖς) and their accidents (συμβεβηκόσιν). But we attribute (ἀνατίθεμεν) neither the flood nor the conflagration to cycles and periods of stars, but say their cause is wickedness (κακία) poured out (χεομένην) more and more and cleansed/purged (καθαιρομένην) by flood or conflagration. And if the prophetic voices (προφητικαὶ φωναί) say that God comes down — the one who said 'Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord' — we interpret figuratively (τροπολογοῦμεν). For God comes down from his own greatness (μέγεθος) and height (ὕψος) when he manages/orders (οἰκονομεῖ) the affairs of men and especially of the wicked. And as usage (συνήθεια) says that teachers come down with (συγκαταβαίνειν) infants (νήπιοι), and the wise or those progressing (προκόπτοντας) with young men just turned (προτραπεῖσιν) to philosophy, not by their bodily coming down, so if anywhere in the divine Scriptures God is said to come down, it is understood analogously (ἀνάλογον) to the usage thus using the word, and so too 'to go up' (ἀναβαίνειν).
pass_b_english: Whether there are cycles, and floods or conflagrations by cycles, or not, and whether our teaching also knows of these things, in many passages and especially where Solomon says, “What is it that has been? The very thing that shall be. And what is it that has been done? The very thing that shall be done” (Ecclesiastes 1:9), and what follows, it is not the present occasion to say. It is enough only to note that Moses and some of the prophets, who were men of the greatest antiquity, did not take from others what they say about the conflagration of the world. Rather, if we must attend to the dates and say so, it was others who misheard them and, not grasping exactly what they said, made up the idea that in each cycle the very same things recur, indistinguishable down to their individual qualities and their accidents.

We, however, ascribe neither the flood nor the conflagration to cycles and periods of the stars. We say that their cause is wickedness, spreading ever further and purged by a flood or a conflagration. And if the prophetic words speak of God coming down, the God who said, “Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord” (Jeremiah 23:24), we take it figuratively. For God comes down from his own greatness and height when he orders the affairs of men, and above all of the wicked. And just as ordinary usage says that teachers come down to little children, and that the wise, or those making progress, come down to young people who have just turned to philosophy, not meaning that they come down bodily, so wherever in the divine Scriptures God is said to come down, it is understood in the same way as this ordinary use of the word; and so too with going up.

choices.choice: ἀνάλογον νοεῖται τῇ οὑτωσὶ χρωμένῃ τῷ ὀνόματι συνηθείᾳ: stiff 'by analogy with the usage that employs the word in this way' made 'in the same way as this ordinary use of the word'
Ecclesiastes 1:9 and Jeremiah 23:24 checked against LXX wording and numbering: correct

Ecclesiastes 1:9 quoted in LXX wording (τί τὸ γεγονός; αὐτὸ τὸ γενησόμενον ...); 'and what follows' points on to 1:9–10 ('nothing new under the sun'). Jeremiah 23:24 (LXX numbering agrees here). ὁ λόγος rendered 'our teaching' (the Christian word/Scripture), not the divine Word. ταυτότητας ... ἀπαραλλάκτους τοῖς ἰδίοις ποιοῖς: Stoic technical language for eternal recurrence (the ἰδίως ποιόν, 'individually qualified' thing); rendered 'the very same things recur, indistinguishable down to their individual qualities and their accidents'. The prophets' words on the conflagration and on God coming down are not specified; possible references, not cited inline: Isaiah 66:15–16; Micah 1:3; Genesis 11:5, 7; Genesis 18:21 (coming down) and Genesis 17:22; 35:13 (going up). 'Wickedness ... purged by a flood' may allude to Genesis 6:5–7; possible only. συγκαταβαίνειν ('come down with/to') is the word behind Christian 'condescension'; rendered 'come down to'. καθαιρομένην rendered 'purged' (wickedness is removed, not itself made clean). ἐκπυ ρώσει (split word) is a staging artefact.
